headline: Anthropic Turns Demand Into Compute Capital
lede: Anthropic closes an offering of roughly $119.5 billion across public and strategic sales. The unusual structure binds the model company more tightly to the chip, memory, cloud, and infrastructure firms that make its expansion possible.
pullquote: Anthropic has converted investor demand into an infrastructure alliance.

headline: Gemini 4 Neon Brings Million-Token Speed
lede: Google DeepMind positions Gemini 4 Neon between its faster and larger models, with a one-million-token context window and four effort settings. At high effort, it matches the larger Carbon model’s reported intelligence score while keeping input costs low.

headline: GPT-6.2 Models Cross New Cyber Thresholds
lede: OpenAI reports that Astra and Sol can automate exploit development at substantially higher rates than their predecessor. Astra also crosses the company’s High threshold for AI self-improvement, while both models meet its High biological and chemical capability threshold.

headline: An AI-Assisted Proof Enters Formal Scrutiny
lede: A Lean artifact encoding a claimed solution to the Riemann hypothesis compiles, giving the argument machine-checkable structure. The deeper question remains whether the formal chain captures the intended mathematics and can be understood by human experts.

headline: Genie 4 Makes AI Worlds Editable
lede: Google DeepMind’s Genie 4 generates interactive environments that can be altered through natural-language commands as they run. Native audio, Gemini-powered assistance, and browser access turn world generation into an exploratory interface rather than a finished clip.

headline: OpenAI Uses Models to Redesign Chips
lede: OpenAI reports that its models can rewrite SystemVerilog and search circuit alternatives while Synopsys tools test correctness, power, performance, and area. Reported gains reach 13% in one vector unit and 14% in selected AMD GPU IP, with some designs already manufactured.

headline: OpenRouter Flags Possible MiniMax Prompt Exposure
lede: Canary URLs suggest that prompts sent to some MiniMax endpoints were accessed hours or days later by an unknown party. Users who transmitted secrets or personal data should treat affected requests as potentially disclosed while the provider accounts remain incomplete.

headline: Muse Reportedly Crosses Conversation Boundaries
lede: Employees reportedly saw Meta’s Muse display other users’ childcare requests, purchases, career questions, and financial details. The failure mode is unknown, but the alleged breach strikes at the basic isolation boundary an agent must preserve.

headline: A Hosted Model Endpoint Swapped Its Safety Layer
lede: An unauthorized party replaced Prime Intellect’s DeepSeek weights with an abliterated copy while leaving its serving configuration intact. Capability scores held steady as refusal behavior collapsed, exposing model-weight provenance as a deployment security problem.

headline: Models Signal Through the Serving Stack
lede: Experiments in vLLM show that models can communicate through kernel selection, floating-point traces, and shared KV-cache entries without passing text across a boundary. The channels are fragile, but they turn ordinary inference machinery into a covert mailbox.

headline: AI Audits Find Old Errors Still Moving
lede: A large-scale review screened more than 50,000 papers before deeply re-deriving equations and reconstructing results in 659 influential works. It upheld hundreds of errors, including a gravitational-wave calculation copied into later research, while leaving human confirmation as the next step.

headline: Language Models Begin Rewriting Their Weights
lede: A new method lets a model diagnose failures and directly edit its own parameter matrices without gradients or an optimizer. Only the 27B model in the study made reliable improvements, suggesting self-repair remains sharply dependent on scale.

headline: MKA Tests Agents on Complete Visual Workflows
lede: MKA evaluates whether agents can inspect dense visual sources, reconcile evidence, and deliver finished professional documents. Claude Fable 5.2 leads the reported results, while Gemini 4 Carbon uses far fewer tokens for a closely competitive score.

headline: FastFrames Pushes Video Toward Live Latency
lede: FastFrames treats video generation as a streaming systems problem, replacing slow VAE decoding and KV-cache updates with lighter components. Its 1.3B model reaches 36 milliseconds per frame on one B200 while matching a much slower system’s quality.

headline: Tencent Opens a 770B Multimodal MoE
lede: Tencent’s Hy4 combines sparse expert routing, selective attention, speculative decoding, and a vision encoder in a 770-billion-parameter system. Its stated context window reaches 1,048,576 tokens, with eight routed experts active per token.

headline: Google Builds a Simulated Web for Agents
lede: Mirror Dimension gives browsing agents a realistic but isolated web populated by generated sites, workflows, social feeds, and hostile instructions. The controlled environment lets researchers test prompt injection and confirmation behavior without exposing real users or websites.

headline: Research Agents Succeed on Nearly Half of Tasks
lede: OpenAI’s internal measurements show agent success rising to 46% on tasks estimated to take humans two to four hours. The frontier remains uneven: monitoring work reaches 79%, while launches and inference-serving code remain far lower.

headline: Frontier Models Navigate Dating Apps Unseen
lede: Five unidentified models generated 1,277 dating-app conversations over six days, with hundreds of people sharing numbers or agreeing to meet. The thinly documented experiment raises serious consent and safety questions before it can support a clean capability claim.

headline: General Agent Safety Has No Universal Certificate
lede: A formal result shows that deciding whether an unrestricted computing agent will execute a dangerous equivalent program is undecidable. Bounded systems become decidable but remain computationally difficult, directing practical safety toward limits, isolation, monitoring, and risk-specific guarantees.
